transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I just keep getting these nagging thoughts. It's like I'm always worrying that I forgot something important. Like, I'll think I left my aunt's medicine out wrong, or maybe I didn't set up my classroom materials safely for the kids. And the thing is, even when I know I probably handled it fine, the doubt just keeps popping back into my head. It's really frustrating.

When you have these worries about forgetting something important, do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like going back to check, asking others for reassurance, or mentally reviewing things—to try to ease that doubt?

Yeah, I do. Um, before I leave the house or my classroom, I’ll usually go back over the same things a few times. Like, I'll physically go back and check the pill organizer, or make sure the stove is off, or look at my lesson plans again. Or I'll just silently replay what I did in my head to make sure I did it right. I basically just keep checking or reviewing it until I finally feel calm enough to actually move on. It's not taking up my entire day or anything, but it does make me run late sometimes.

Have you always been this way—checking things and worrying about doing tasks perfectly since you were younger—or is this something that started more recently and feels different from how you used to be?

I'm not really sure, honestly. I mean, I think I've always been a little careful about things, maybe double-checking my homework when I was in school, but it never felt like this. This feels... different. It's like I can't just check once and be done with it anymore. So I guess it feels more recent, or at least it's gotten more noticeable lately.

Besides these concerns about safety-checking and doing things correctly, do you also find yourself excessively worrying about other areas of your life—like your finances, health, or relationships—even when there's no specific checking behavior involved?

No, not really. I mean, I worry about normal things like anyone else—paying bills on time or hoping I don't get sick—but it's not like the checking. Once I pay a bill, I know it's paid. I don't sit there obsessing over it or wondering if I did it wrong. It's really just the safety stuff and making sure I didn't mess up something important that gets stuck in my head.
On an average day, about how much total time would you say you spend on these checking and reviewing behaviors, and how distressing is it when you can't complete them?

Um, well, like I said, it's not taking up my whole day. I'd say maybe... an hour total, spread out? It's just those few minutes here and there before I leave the house or when I'm packing up my classroom. I just have to go back and check the pill organizer, or make sure the stove is off, or look over my lesson plans again. Sometimes I just replay it in my head. If I can't do it, or if I try to just walk away, I get this really uncomfortable, anxious feeling in my chest. It's like I can't focus on anything else until I go back and check it until I feel calm enough to move on. It's frustrating because it does make me run late, but I just can't seem to stop myself from doing it.

When you're in the moment checking the pill organizer or stove, do you feel like these worries and checking are excessive or unreasonable, or does it feel like a completely justified response to a real risk?

I mean... logically, I know it's excessive. Like, I know I just turned the stove off. But in that exact moment, the "what if" just feels so strong. It feels like a real risk right then, so checking feels like the only way to be completely safe. It's really only after I finally walk away that I look back and realize how silly it is to check the exact same thing three or four times.
